explicit_propositions.text: We leave Washington, D.C., early each year before the August recess.
Congress does not pass a formal budget annually; instead, it uses Continuing Resolutions (CRs).
A Continuing Resolution maintains prior levels of government spending without requiring justification.
The August recess lasts approximately one month.
The federal government spends money it does not have and prints more currency to cover deficits.
Passing a full budget would require Congress to justify individual spending programs and projects.
Some funded projects mentioned in budgets may no longer exist.
Schools, churches, local governments, states, businesses, and families all use budgets.
The U.S. Constitution requires Congress to pass a budget annually.
The United States has failed to pass a formal budget for nearly 30 years.

assumptions.text: Budgeting is a fundamental marker of fiscal responsibility and rational governance.
Failure to pass a budget reflects systemic incompetence and moral failure among elected officials.
Continuing Resolutions enable wasteful and unaccountable spending by avoiding scrutiny.
The Speaker of the House lacks consistent control over the Republican majority due to internal instability.
Elected representatives prioritize personal convenience and political rituals over legislative duty.
The current system allows powerful figures like Speaker Pelosi to perpetuate poor financial policies.
Public awareness of congressional dysfunction will lead voters to demand accountability.
The upcoming election offers a critical opportunity to restore conservative principles in Congress.
The President’s cognitive decline undermines his ability to govern effectively and responsibly.
Evangelical Christian voters’ absence in previous elections directly contributed to Democratic electoral success.
